title: Interpretable machine learning models for the prediction of all-cause mortality and time to death in hemodialysis patients.
summary: The primary full-text record describes a 359-patient retrospective hemodialysis cohort and evaluated ML mortality/time-to-death predictions; this supports a specific clinical prediction study, not clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Random forest, support-vector machine and logistic-regression models predict all-cause mortality; random-forest regression estimates time to death, with SHAP factor interpretation.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: In 359 hemodialysis patients, the optimized full-variable random forest had mortality AUROC 0.86±0.07 (sensitivity 0.86, specificity 0.75); a 22-variable model had AUROC 0.80±0.06.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective single-cohort prediction does not establish improved survival or generalization to other dialysis populations.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest, support-vector machine and logistic-regression models predict all-cause mortality; random-forest regression estimates time to death, with SHAP factor interpretation.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
